summary: One lens shows how two explosive speeds reshape a wave; then all of them merge into one inward wave.

paragraphs.text: All {{detonators}} detonators fire together, and each sets off an expanding wave inside its own explosive lens. Left alone, these waves would arrive as a patchwork of bumps, not as one clean squeeze.

Each lens is built from two explosives that burn at different speeds. A slower insert sits in the path of the wave and holds back its middle. The front flattens, then bends the other way, much as a glass lens bends light.

Where the lenses meet, the {{detonators}} shaped waves join into a single sphere that moves inward. It reaches the pusher after {{implosion_time}}. The lens shapes here are illustrative, not measured.

events.detail: The slow insert holds back the middle of the wave.
{{detonators}} shaped fronts join into one converging sphere.

callouts.text: {{detonators}} detonators fire together. Each one starts its own wave, spreading outward. The core needs one wave moving inward.
In the fast explosive, the wave spreads from the detonator as a bulging arc.
The slow insert holds the middle of the wave back, so the front flattens.
Past the insert the front curves the other way, bowed toward the centre of the sphere.
The {{detonators}} fronts merge into one smooth sphere, shrinking inward.
